issue.title: Azure Monitor: Refresh metrics resource types

labels.name: user-099404c7/repo-84c5969e
labels.description: This PR is from external contributor

issue.body:
<!--

Thank you for sending a pull request! Here are some tips:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contribution guide at https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

2. Ensure you include and run the appropriate tests as part of your Pull Request.

3. In a new feature or configuration option, an update to the documentation is necessary. Everything related to the documentation is under the docs folder in the root of the repository.

4. If the Pull Request is a work in progress, make use of GitHub's "Draft PR" feature and mark it as such.

5. If you can not merge your Pull Request due to a merge conflict, Rebase it. This gets it in sync with the main branch.

6. Name your PR as "<FeatureArea>: Describe your change", e.g. Alerting: Prevent race condition. If it's a fix or feature relevant for the changelog describe the user impact in the title. The PR title is used to auto-generate the changelog for issues marked with the "add to changelog" label.

7. If your PR content should be added to the What's New document for the next major or minor release, add the **add to what's new** label to your PR. Note that you should add this label to the main PR that introduces the feature; do not add this label to smaller PRs for the feature.

-->

**What is this feature?**

Users can select 12 additional Azure resource types in the Metrics picker when namespace sampling misses their type. This refresh includes the original Edge Machines fix and 11 more types checked against public metrics and ARM references.

The resources must still be visible to the datasource through Resource Graph.

**Why do we need this feature?**

The picker combines a static list with namespaces found in sampled scopes. A supported type missing from both sources is filtered out before a user can select it.

This refresh closes confirmed catalog gaps without changing resource discovery or metric execution.

**Who is this feature for?**

Azure Monitor datasource users who query metrics for newer resource types.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

<!--

- Automatically closes linked issue when the Pull Request is merged.

Usage: "Fixes #<issue number>", or "Fixes (paste link of issue)"

-->

Related to #135527. This is a fallback-list refresh, not a complete fix for resource discovery. The general discovery fix is in #135542.

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Production changes are limited to resource-type entries and display names. Existing entries, labels, and multi-resource compatibility flags are unchanged. Backend changes are tests only.

This PR adds the following 12 resource types, including Edge Machines. Each has a nonempty public metric table and a public ARM resource reference:

| Resource type | Public evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `microsoft.app/sessionpools` | [Metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics/microsoft-app-sessionpools-metrics), [ARM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.app/sessionpools) |
| `microsoft.azurestackhci/edgemachines` | [Metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics/microsoft-azurestackhci-edgemachines-metrics), [ARM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.azurestackhci/edgemachines) |
| `microsoft.durabletask/schedulers` | [Metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics/microsoft-durabletask-schedulers-metrics), [ARM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.durabletask/2026-02-01/schedulers) |
| `microsoft.horizondb/clusters` | [Metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics/microsoft-horizondb-clusters-metrics), [ARM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.horizondb/clusters) |
| `microsoft.iotfirmwaredefense/workspaces` | [Metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics/microsoft-iotfirmwaredefense-workspaces-metrics), [ARM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.iotfirmwaredefense/2025-08-02/workspaces) |
| `microsoft.managednetworkfabric/networkfabriccontrollers` | [Metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics/microsoft-managednetworkfabric-networkfabriccontrollers-metrics), [ARM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.managednetworkfabric/networkfabriccontrollers) |
| `microsoft.managednetworkfabric/networkfabrics` | [Metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics/microsoft-managednetworkfabric-networkfabrics-metrics), [ARM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.managednetworkfabric/networkfabrics) |
| `microsoft.monitor/pipelinegroups` | [Metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics/microsoft-monitor-pipelinegroups-metrics), [ARM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.monitor/2023-10-01-preview/pipelinegroups) |
| `microsoft.network/networksecurityperimeters` | [Metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics/microsoft-network-networksecurityperimeters-metrics), [ARM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.network/networksecurityperimeters) |
| `microsoft.openenergyplatform/energyservices` | [Metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics/microsoft-openenergyplatform-energyservices-metrics), [ARM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.openenergyplatform/energyservices) |
| `microsoft.quantum/provideraccounts` | [Metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics/microsoft-quantum-provideraccounts-metrics), [ARM tag support](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/tag-support#microsoftquantum), [ARM permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/permissions/compute#microsoftquantum) |
| `oracle.database/goldengatedeployments` | [Metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics/oracle-database-goldengatedeployments-metrics), [ARM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/oracle.database/goldengatedeployments) |

Quantum's ARM status is corroborated by public tag-support and RBAC references and the live tenant-level provider API, not only its metrics table. No new preview-gated or virtual-only catalog entries are included. Some included services or metrics have Azure-side preview or availability restrictions; this change does not bypass those restrictions.

This is a current-catalog comparison, not a claim to reconstruct exact introduction dates or cover every Azure metrics type. It does not claim to fix "No data" after Advanced entry. Live Resource Graph visibility and end-to-end picker selection were not verified.

The tests use shared metadata, picker utility, and URL-builder suites. There is no per-resource test file. The backend tests retain the earlier empty/sparse-response checks, including zero versus null or missing Average samples.

**Validation**

- Passed: 5 frontend suites, 133 tests, with the standard plugin setup. The original 10 catalog-refresh cases failed before their metadata update. The Quantum case then failed separately before its addition, with the other 11 metadata cases passing.

```powershell
yarn jest --config public\app\plugins\datasource\azuremonitor\jest.config.js --no-watch --runInBand --silent --runTestsByPath public\app\plugins\datasource\azuremonitor\azureMetadata\resourceTypes.test.ts public\app\plugins\datasource\azuremonitor\resourcePicker\resourcePickerData.test.ts public\app\plugins\datasource\azuremonitor\azure_resource_graph\azure_resource_graph_datasource.test.ts public\app\plugins\datasource\azuremonitor\components\ResourcePicker\utils.test.ts public\app\plugins\datasource\azuremonitor\azure_monitor\url_builder.test.ts
```

- Passed: targeted ESLint, Prettier, and whitespace checks.

```powershell
node node_modules\eslint\bin\eslint.js public\app\plugins\datasource\azuremonitor\azureMetadata\resourceTypes.ts public\app\plugins\datasource\azuremonitor\azureMetadata\resourceTypes.test.ts
node node_modules\prettier\bin\prettier.cjs --check public\app\plugins\datasource\azuremonitor\azureMetadata\resourceTypes.ts public\app\plugins\datasource\azuremonitor\azureMetadata\resourceTypes.test.ts
git diff --check
```

- Passed: independent preservation checks confirmed the approved additions, no removals or existing label changes, and unchanged multi-resource compatibility flags. The fallback now contains 262 types, including exactly one Quantum provider-account entry.
- Failed: plugin type-check, with 215 diagnostic lines byte-identical to the preserved clean-base log. Neither changed metadata file has a diagnostic.

```powershell
node node_modules\typescript\bin\tsc --noEmit --pretty false --project public\app\plugins\datasource\azuremonitor\tsconfig.json
```

- Previously passed; not rerun for this metadata-only refresh: the full Metrics backend package. Its test-only changes are unchanged.

```powershell
go test .\pkg\tsdb\azuremonitor\metrics -count=1
```

**Post-deploy checks**

Proposed owner: the deploying Azure Monitor datasource maintainer. After rollout, check accessible examples of the added types in Resource Graph and the picker, including when namespace sampling misses them. Confirm resource-scoped metadata loads and retain a working VM as a control.

For the first 24 hours, watch existing datasource error/latency dashboards and request traces for `Microsoft.ResourceGraph/resources`, `metricNamespaces`, and `metricDefinitions`. Healthy results are correct resource identities, successful metadata loads, and unchanged control behavior. If this catalog change causes query failures or picker regressions, revert the catalog-refresh commit. No new monitoring infrastructure is introduced.

Please check that:
- [ ] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
- [ ] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [ ] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-whats-new), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/) doc.

issue.title: E2E: Remove tests for externalized datasources
issue.body:
**What is this feature?**

This PR removes the externalized datasource plugins' E2E tests.

**Why do we need this feature?**

Now that these plugins are external, running their E2E tests triggers a download from the catalog. Removing their tests removes downloading plugins over the internet as a source of flakiness.

**Who is this feature for?**

Grafana developers

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

N/A

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

The externalized plugins have E2E tests in their respective repositories, and there is a [test datasource](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/tree/main/e2e-playwright/test-plugins/grafana-test-datasource) with E2E tests covering general functionality.

Azure Monitor and Graphite are still part of the core Grafana codebase at this time; their E2E tests will be removed along with their code in the near future.

Please check that:
- [ ] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
- [ ] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [ ] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-whats-new), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/) doc.

-- **Grafana permissions:** `Organization administrator` role.

+- **Server access:** Shell access to the host running Grafana, with permission to write to the plugin directory and restart Grafana.

-If you're provisioning the data source, you also need administrative rights on the server hosting your Grafana instance.
+## Install the data source
+
+The Parca data source has both a frontend and a Go backend, so you must build both and then copy the result into your Grafana plugin directory.
+
+### Build the data source from source
+
+Clone the repository and build the frontend and backend:
+
+```sh
+git clone https://github.com/grafana/grafana-parca-datasource.git
+cd grafana-parca-datasource
+npm ci
+npm run build
+go run github.com/magefile/mage -v buildAll
+```
+
+Both build commands are required. `npm run build` produces the frontend assets, and the `mage buildAll` target compiles the backend executables for each supported platform. Running only `npm run build` produces a data source that Grafana loads but can't query, because the backend executable is missing.
+
+Both commands write their output to the `dist/` directory.
+
+### Deploy the data source to Grafana
+
+Copy the contents of `dist/` into a `parca` directory inside your Grafana plugin directory. On a package-based Linux installation, the plugin directory is `/var/lib/grafana/plugins`:
+
+```sh
+sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/grafana/plugins/parca
+sudo cp -a dist/. /var/lib/grafana/plugins/parca/
+sudo chown -R grafana:grafana /var/lib/grafana/plugins/parca
+```
+
+The Grafana process must be able to read every file in the directory and execute the backend binary.
+
+If you run Grafana in Docker, mount the `dist/` directory at `/var/lib/grafana/plugins/parca` instead:
+
+```sh
+docker run -d \
+  -v "$(pwd)/dist:/var/lib/grafana/plugins/parca" \
+  -e GF_PLUGINS_ALLOW_LOADING_UNSIGNED_PLUGINS=parca \
+  -p 3000:3000 \
+  grafana/grafana:latest
+```
+
+The plugin directory path is set by the `plugins` configuration option. If you've changed it, use your configured path instead. For more information, refer to [Configure Grafana](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/<GRAFANA_VERSION>/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/#plugins).
+
+### Allow the unsigned plugin
+
+A data source you build yourself isn't signed, and Grafana refuses to load unsigned plugins by default. Add the `parca` plugin ID to the `allow_loading_unsigned_plugins` option in your Grafana configuration file, typically `/etc/grafana/grafana.ini`:
+
+```ini
+[plugins]
+allow_loading_unsigned_plugins = parca
+```
+
+Restart Grafana to load the data source:
+
+```sh
+sudo systemctl restart grafana-server
+```
+
+When Grafana loads an unsigned plugin, it writes a warning to the server log:
+
+```text
+WARN[...] Permitting unsigned plugin. This is not recommended   pluginId=parca
+```
+
+For more information, refer to [Plugin signatures](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/<GRAFANA_VERSION>/administration/plugin-management/plugin-sign/) and the [`allow_loading_unsigned_plugins` option](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/<GRAFANA_VERSION>/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/#allow_loading_unsigned_plugins).
+
+### Verify the data source loaded
+
+To confirm Grafana loaded the Parca data source:
+
+1. Click **Connections** in the left-side menu.
+1. Click **Add new connection**.
+1. Type `Parca` in the search bar.
+
+If **Parca** doesn't appear, check the Grafana server log for plugin loading errors. Refer to [Troubleshoot Parca data source issues](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/<GRAFANA_VERSION>/datasources/parca/troubleshooting/#installation-issues).
+
+### Migrate from the bundled data source
+
+Grafana 13.1 and earlier bundled the Parca data source. If you're upgrading from one of those versions and you already have Parca data sources configured, install it as described in the preceding sections before you upgrade Grafana. The plugin ID is still `parca`, so your existing data sources continue to work once Grafana can load it.

If they're installing external Parca before upgrading to 13.2+, they would also need to add this to their `grafana.ini` to make sure that it overrides the bundled version:

```
[parca]
as_external = true
```

issue.title: Cloudwatch PromQL queries do not return data in alert rules
issue.body:
**What happened**:

Cloudwatch PromQL queries that return data in Explore have no output when used in an alert rule.

**What you expected to happen**:

The query should have the same output in Explore and when used in an alert rule.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

1. Go to Explore
2. Choose a Cloudwatch datasource
3. Select `CloudWatch Metrics` and `PromQL` at the top of the query editor
4. Run a query that outputs data
5. Create an alert rule using the same datasource and PromQL query
6. Run `Preview alert rule condition` in the alert editor (or save the alert) and check the output

**Anything else we need to know?**:

Provisioned alerts that include `type: promqlQuery` work as expected. When created in the UI, the alert's `queryLanguage` is set to CWLI and `type` is absent.

**Environment**:

- Grafana version: 13.3.0-38260622283
- Plugin version: 12.11.1
- User OS & Browser: MacOS & Google Chrome
